headline: The one run back had genuine range top to bottom, but it's still a single data point. No second run yet to confirm a rhythm. The threshold reading is now the oldest thing on the board.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is a large, intact aerobic base sitting under a very quiet loading side. The recent four weeks of running mileage were dominated by a big block of long, low-HR time on feet, which inflates the volume totals but represents durability work rather than sharpening. Since then running has thinned to one session — a genuinely varied effort that touched all the way up — and strength has stayed sporadic rather than establishing any cadence. Steps remain high even on rest days, so background movement is doing real work keeping the engine warm despite the training-log gap. The cardio-load status reads as detraining, which reflects the recent absence of logged sessions more than any loss of underlying fitness; treat it as a load signal, not a fitness verdict. The honest read: you're carrying a deep base with a temporarily idle top layer, and the last run is the first sign of the layer coming back online.
sections.trends: Year-to-date the trajectory is strongly ahead of last year — you've banked several times the distance you had at this point in 2025, so the macro shape is clearly building over the long horizon. Zoomed into the 16-week view, the recent shape is a large durability spike followed by a trough, which is normal after a trail-heavy block and consistent with your year-round, non-periodised approach rather than a single-peak plan. That cyclical rise-and-settle is coherent with your standing goals — the concern isn't the trough itself, it's how long it lasts before the next consistent stretch begins.
sections.threshold: The threshold and VO2max readings are the weakest part of the current picture, not because they've regressed but because they're stale — the last genuine threshold marker predates the entire recent block. Nothing in the recent running challenges or refreshes it; the long trail efforts sat far below threshold and the one recent quality run, while it reached the top end briefly, wasn't a sustained tempo. Practically, your true current threshold is unverified. The base to support a strong reading is almost certainly there; it simply hasn't been tested.
sections.zones: The weekly zone aggregate is heavily skewed toward the very bottom, which is exactly right for the durability block that dominated it — hours of low, steady time on feet is what that work is supposed to look like. The standout in the per-session shapes is the single recent run: a clean spread from easy through to a brief top-end touch, which is the first session in weeks with any meaningful time above the aerobic floor. For a hybrid athlete that's a healthy re-entry — but one such session doesn't rebalance a block that's otherwise been almost entirely floor-level. The distribution needs a genuine sustained middle-to-upper effort to serve the speed side of your capacity.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength HR shapes look normal for functional work — mostly low zone with occasional pushes into the middle, which is expected when no continuous cardiovascular demand is present. The most recent lift logged no HR at all, so there's a gap there. Nothing in the source agreement is out of line; the recent run's HR responded cleanly across the range, which is a reassuring sign the engine is answering when asked.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the real story better than any single metric: a dense, clustered block of activity followed by a genuine off-stretch, now interrupted by one run and a handful of scattered lifts. The pattern is feast-then-quiet rather than steady — which is fine occasionally, but the streak counters sitting at zero on both running and strength underline that no repeatable weekly frame is currently in place. The next two weeks are where that either re-forms or stays fragmented.
sections.personal_bests: None of your speed PBs are within reach off the current state — they were set at sharp, race-specific fitness and the recent block was durability, not speed. The ultra-distance bests, by contrast, are well underpinned by the base you've been laying down. If you want a shot at the shorter-distance marks this season, the sharpening work to support them hasn't started yet; that's a deliberate choice, not a gap to panic about.

watch_items: Watch whether a second and third run land this week — one run doesn't yet distinguish a restart from an isolated session.
Watch for a sustained tempo or threshold effort to finally refresh the oldest metric on the board.
Watch whether strength moves from scattered singles to an actual weekly frame.
Watch whether the next lift captures HR, since the most recent one logged none.
